name: On-base plus slugging (ops)
title: OPS Calculator (On-Base Plus Slugging)
desc: Calculate your on-base plus slugging (OPS), on-base percentage (OBP), slugging percentage (SLG), and batting average (BA) using our OPS calculator.

c: Fill in the fields below to instantly see the player’s calculated offensive stats.

m.h: Total number of safe hits (1B + 2B + 3B + HR).
1B: One-base hits.
2B: Two-base hits.
3B: Three-base hits.
HR: Four-base hits.
BB: Bases on balls.
HBP: Number of times hit by a pitch.
AB: Official times at bat (excludes walks, hit by pitch, and sacrifices).
SF: Batted fly outs that allowed a runner to score.

c: OPS performance grade Grade A+ (MVP Caliber): You are an elite superstar dominating the league.
OPS performance grade Grade A (Excellent): You are an All-Star caliber hitter delivering top-tier offensive value.
OPS performance grade Grade B+ (Very Good): You are a highly reliable hitter performing well above league average.
OPS performance grade Grade B (Above average): You are a solid offensive contributor, providing steady production.
OPS performance grade Grade C (Average): You are a dependable hitter offering typical league-average results.
OPS performance grade Grade D (Below average): You may be struggling and need to make adjustments.
OPS performance grade Grade E (Poor): You are in a deep slump with critical offensive challenges.
OPS performance grade Grade F (Very Poor): You are facing major difficulties making an impact at the plate.

eq.formula: OBP = (H + BB + HBP)/(AB + BB + HBP + SF)

var.f: AB*OBP + BB*OBP - BB + HBP*OBP - HBP + OBP*SF

c: Onim Example 1: How much weight will I lose if I stay in a sauna for 30 minutes, burning 500 kcal/hour?
Onim Example 2: What are the calories burned per hour if I stay in a sauna for 90 minutes, and burn 1000 kcal?
Onim Example 3: How long do I need to stay in a sauna to lose 800 kcal if I burn 400 kcal/hour?

How the result is calculated: Divide the time in the sauna in minutes by 60: 0.5. Multiply the last result by the calories burned per hour: 250. Divide the previous value by 7700 (energy stored in 1 kg of body fat): 0.03247 kg = 0.07158 lb.
How the result is calculated: Divide the time in the sauna in minutes by 60: 1.5. Divide the calories burned by the last result: 666.7 kcal/hour.
How the result is calculated: Divide the calories burned by the calories burned per hour: 2. Multiply the last result by 60 min: 120 min.

m.h: In some sports ties are counted as half a win (American football - put 0.5 in here), while in others their as good as a loss (soccer, aka real football - put 0)

c: How the result is calculated: Divide the number of wins by the number of games: 58/82 = 0.7073 Multiply the last result by 100: 70.73%.

How the result is calculated: Multiply the number of tie games by 0.5: 2 × 0.5 = 1 Add this result to the number of wins: 13. Divide the last result by the number of games: 13/17 = 0.7647 Multiply the last result by 100: 76.47%.

desc: Bertrand's paradox is an intriguing warning for every scientist: dealing with infinity and randomness can lead to pitfalls!

c: Consider the equilateral triangle inscribed in a circle. What is the probability that a randomly chosen chord is longer than the side of the triangle?

In the random endpoints method we build the chord by defining its endpoints. Imagine fixing one endpoint in one of triangle's vertexes. What is the chance that a randomly generated cord from this situation is longer than the triangle's side? Take a look at the image below, and try your luck (or math)!

Consider a triangle's side and the radius of the circle perpendicular to it. What is the probability of a chord parallel to the side with midpoint on the radius being longer than the side? Take a look at the image below, and try your math!

Every chord is uniquely identified by its midpoint. Given a random point in the circle, what is the chance that the chord with such point as midpoint is longer than the inscribed triangle's side? Make a guess after taking a look at the picture below!

Correct answer! Each point that falls in the circle inscribed in the triangle is the midpoint of a chord longer than the side of the triangle. The inscribed circle has radius equal to half the original circle's radius, hence its area is 1/4 of the larger circle's area. The ratio of the areas gives us the probability of the chord being longer than the side: 25%. This is not all! Try other values in
